name: Scourge Flare

stars.name: The Lash
stars.notes: Extreme flare star. Produces superflare events up to 10,000 times baseline luminosity on irregular cycles averaging 11 days. Surface magnetic field topology is violently unstable.

planets.name: Scar Tissue
planets.notes: Tidally locked. The dayside surface has been repeatedly sterilized and re-melted by superflare events. Nightside shows evidence of past atmospheric freeze-out.

planets.name: Whiplash
planets.notes: Once may have held liquid water. Repeated flare events have stripped the atmosphere multiple times over geological history. Surface is a wasteland of oxidized iron and shattered basalt.

planets.name: Flagellant
planets.notes: Thin residual nitrogen atmosphere that is periodically ablated by flare events and slowly re-accumulates from volcanic outgassing. A world trapped in a cycle of destruction and partial recovery.

planets.name: The Penitent
planets.notes: Frozen world at the outer edge. Even at this distance, superflare events cause measurable surface sublimation. Ice cliffs bear stratified layers of melt-refreeze cycles like geological scars.

anomalies.name: The Scourging
anomalies.location: Entire system, originating from The Lash
anomalies.notes: Irregular superflare events increase system radiation levels by four orders of magnitude for hours at a time. No reliable prediction method exists. Danger level: catastrophic during events, high at baseline.

anomalies.name: Magnetic Tempest Zone
anomalies.location: Inner system within 0.5 AU of The Lash
anomalies.notes: The Lash's chaotic magnetic field creates zones of violent magnetic reconnection that generate secondary particle bursts independent of flare events. Navigation instruments become unreliable. Danger level: extreme.

anomalies.name: Whiplash Ozone Phantom
anomalies.notes: During flare events, Whiplash's residual surface volatiles are ionized into a brief, blinding atmospheric glow that saturates optical sensors. Danger level: high for optical navigation.

asteroid_belts.name: The Flayed Belt
asteroid_belts.composition: silicate and iron fragments, heavily irradiated
asteroid_belts.notes: Radiation-blasted remnants of what may have been a larger body disrupted by tidal interactions. Surface materials show extreme radiation damage at the molecular level.

stations.name: Flare Watch Epsilon
stations.location: Outer system, 12 AU from The Lash, radiation-hardened orbit
stations.notes: Automated stellar monitoring station studying flare prediction models. Designed to survive superflare events. Fourth generation unit; predecessors destroyed during flares exceeding design parameters.

faction_control.notes: Unclaimed. The Ember Verge Astronomical Consortium maintains the Flare Watch station for academic purposes only.

history: Scourge Flare was identified as a flare star of unusual violence in 2498 when a routine survey detected a superflare visible at interstellar distances. The event's energy output exceeded any previously recorded M-dwarf flare by a factor of twelve.

The research vessel 'Patient Observer' established a monitoring position in the outer system in 2523. During a superflare event that exceeded all projections, the vessel's radiation shielding failed. The crew of six survived but suffered severe radiation illness; two died during the return journey.

Three generations of automated monitoring stations have been destroyed by flare events that exceeded their design tolerances. The current fourth-generation station, Flare Watch Epsilon, incorporates hardening derived from military warship specifications.
description: Scourge Flare is dominated by The Lash, an M4V red dwarf with the temperament of a bomb. Its magnetic field is in constant violent flux, producing superflare events of staggering power on cycles that resist prediction. During a scourging event, the system's radiation levels spike by four orders of magnitude, sterilizing surfaces, stripping atmospheres, and overwhelming shielding rated for far harsher stars. Between events, the system simmers at elevated radiation levels that would be considered dangerous in any other context but here represent the calm.

The four worlds of Scourge Flare bear the geological record of billions of years of abuse. Scar Tissue's dayside has been melted so many times its surface is glassy slag. Whiplash's atmosphere has been stripped and partially rebuilt in a cycle repeated thousands of times. Flagellant exists in a state of perpetual almost-recovery, its thin atmosphere accumulating between scourgings only to be torn away again. Even distant Penitent shows layered ice scars from flare-driven sublimation events.

The scientific value of Scourge Flare lies in understanding extreme stellar behavior—flare prediction could save lives on colonies orbiting less violent but still active M-dwarfs throughout settled space. This has justified the continued deployment of automated monitoring stations despite the repeated loss of hardware. No crewed mission has returned to the system since the Patient Observer incident, and the Ember Verge Astronomical Consortium has no plans to authorize one.
